display.title: Episode 453: Reb Ariel and the Lion
display.summary_short: A young listener's letter about dancing at Hakafos, Shema with a Beis Yaakov class, and the story of Reb Ariel, guarded all Shabbos by a lion in the wilderness.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi celebrates the show's ninth year and 453 weeks on the air, then reads a five-year-old's letter about Simchas Torah: riding on his father's shoulders, dancing with a little Torah while the crowd spilled into the street, and treats at Hakafos. Uncle Yossi reminds everyone to do mitzvos with joy. After the Hakochainik march, a second-grade class from Beis Yaakov of Boro Park recites the Shema, and everyone gives tzedakah. In the story, little Devorah comes home on Friday, helps her mother prepare for Shabbos, and retells her teacher's story: Reb Ariel refuses to travel with a caravan on Shabbos and is left alone in the wilderness, where a huge lion sent by Hashem guards him all Shabbos and then carries him to the caravan, which had been attacked by wild animals. The travelers ask forgiveness and make him their leader. Uncle Yossi then urges children to learn and say the Twelve Pesukim every day, offers free copies, and gives candle-lighting time.
display.lesson: One who guards Shabbos is guarded by Shabbos, and Hashem protects those who think of Him every day.

date.note: Candle time 4:19 fits Friday 16 November 1990 in New York, one week after episode 452 (4:25); a Simchas Torah letter is read a few weeks after the Yom Tov.

advisories.note: A traveler is left alone in the wilderness; the caravan is attacked by wild animals but survives.
